9-- Added `BudgetSummary`, `SectionCost`, `ProvenanceBlock` and `ProvenanceEntry`: plain types for a response-level budget report and a provenance block, with builder methods, camelCase `serde::Serialize` behind the `serde` feature and `schemars::JsonSchema` behind `schemars`. They are not attached to `AgentResponse` yet.
10-- michi-core: `AgentResponse` keeps its body in one list of sections. `items()` and `kv_items()` are shorthand that append a section named for the response's type, so calling both renders both bodies in call order instead of silently dropping one, as long as their root keys differ. Every section is a root key of the document: a repeated key (two `items()` calls, two `kv_items()` with a shared key, a name like `budget`, a repeated provenance label) renders the `toon_validation_failed` error naming the key, with `isError` true, instead of invalid TOON. For several lists use `.section(Section::toon(distinct_name, ..))`. The same applies to `@orin-dx/michi`'s `items()` and `kvItems()`, which render one list per response. A `Text` section now renders as one escaped string value (`name: "..."`), not raw prose.
11-
12-  Breaking: removed `AgentResponse::render_toon()`, `render_kv()`, `total_count()` and `truncation()`, and NAPI `renderToon()`, `renderKv()` and `totalCount()`. A response with only `items()` or `kv_items()` renders the same text, with these exceptions: a `totalCount` line renders only when the total is larger than the rows returned (so an empty list no longer prints `totalCount: 0`), and `render(Json)` / `structuredContent` gain a `sections` array next to `body`.
13-
14-  Migration: `AgentResponse::new(..).items(..).hints(..).render_toon()` becomes `.render(OutputFormat::Text)`; `.total_count(n)` becomes `Section::toon(name, fields, rows).total_count(Some(n))` passed to `.section(..)`; `.items(rows, f).truncation(&outcome, g)` becomes `.truncated_section(Section::toon(name, f, rows), &outcome, g)`. In JavaScript, `renderToon()` and `renderKv()` become `renderText()`, and `totalCount(n)` becomes the optional third argument of `items(rows, fields, n)` (second of `kvItems(items, n)`).
15-- `PartialSuccess` reports each operation's position in your batch, so `results[i]` and `ops[i]` stay aligned in the rendered output. `completed` and `skipped` are `Vec<OpRef>`, a new type with `index`, `operation` and an optional `reason` (a machine token such as `budget_exhausted`), and `FailedOp` gains `index`.
16-
17-  Breaking: the rendered report changes. `completed[2]: a,b` becomes a table, `completed[2]{index,operation}:` with one `0,a` row per op, and `failed` and `skipped` are `{index,operation,reason}` tables too. A skipped op with no reason renders `null` in that column. Anything that parses the old text must read the new tables. In Rust, build the vectors from `OpRef::new(index, operation)` (add `.reason(token)` for a skipped op) instead of strings, and pass the index as the first argument of `FailedOp::new(index, operation, reason)`. In Node, `renderPartialSuccess` takes `{ index, operation, reason? }` objects for `completed` and `skipped` instead of strings, and each `FailedOp` needs an `index`.

A response now renders its sections, then `budget:`, `provenance:`, `help[]` and `recovery[]`; the per-section roll-up under `budget:` appears only when the response has two or more sections. `render(Json)` and `to_call_tool_result().structured_content` gain `sections`, `budget` and `provenance` keys, present only when set (a response with no section, budget or provenance keeps exactly `body`, `hints`, `recovery` and `isError`). - **`+regex:`/`-regex:` (closes #8).** The modifier applies to the regex term. Rejected: leaving the degrade to an optional literal, which ranked the files a `-regex:` meant to exclude.
- **Quoted regex.** `regex:"a b"` already lexed as one pattern; only the README lacked it. No new syntax.
- **`--language` goes by file extension.** The TypeScript analyzer owns all eight extensions, so the filter compares the path extension. Rejected: a `LanguageId::JavaScript` variant, which would split one analyzer for a filter.
- **Declaration and test files.** `.d.mts`/`.d.cts` are skipped like `.d.ts`; `.test`/`.spec` cover every analyzable extension.
- **Empty quoted phrase.** `""` produces no term, like an empty query, so `foo ""` behaves as `foo` and `""` alone gets the no-positive-terms diagnostic.

## 25. Removed public types nothing builds or consumes (2026-11-06)

- **Removed.** The core result types no longer derive `Serialize` or `Deserialize` (wire shapes live in the output layer; `Digest` keeps its hand-written impls). `SearchResponse` stores counts only; the output layer words the truncation hint. Gone from the code: `SearchOptions`, `SearchLimits` and `From<&SearchLimits> for Budget`, `SymbolsResult` and its projection, `DependentsResult`, `ExtractRequest`, `WorkspaceOptions`, `TsconfigMode`, the `Rust`/`Python`/`Go`/`Java` `LangData` variants with their `*Data` structs, `RustPathAnchor`, `DependencyTarget::RustPath`/`Namespace`, `BindingKind::NamespaceWide`, `ErrorContext`, the `MonoklError` variants with no constructor (`TokenizerInit`, `Json`, `PathOutsideRoot`, `StaleDiskCache`, `InvalidGitRef`, `Git`, `SymlinkRejected`, `FileTooLarge`, `LockPoisoned`) and `FileIoError`'s `Write`, `CreateDir` and `Remove`. `serde_json` is a dev-dependency.
- **Why.** AGENTS.md forbids pre-rendered truncation strings and serializable core types, and the "wire or don't define" rule asks for a call site in the same change. Nothing called these; a public type without a caller promises behavior nothing tests, and `#[non_exhaustive]` makes adding a variant later a non-breaking change.
- **The spec text stays the design.** Parts 1 to 3 still describe these items; each returns, with its spec text as the starting point, in the change that adds the command or module that constructs it. The architecture docs say which are absent.
- **Rejected.** Keeping them as future API: they would stay public, untested and unconsumed, and the first real caller would likely need a different shape (the spec's own `SearchLimits` is already superseded by Part 8).

## 26. Search rows show the matching lines (2026-11-07)

- **Decision.** Each `search` row gains a `snippet` cell: the lines of the block that matched, numbered, at most three, each cut at 160 characters, with the rest counted. The block's first line is left out when the block has a signature, because that column shows it. (Refined by §44: a line is left out when it lies inside the signature's head, wherever it is.)
- **Why.** Rows held only a location and a signature, so an agent had to read the file to see why a block matched, a second turn the tool exists to save. Against pinned zustand, zod and axios, the declaration's own line was in the output for 15 of 59 identifiers before and 59 of 59 after (`just rg-compare`); output grew about 1.7x and stays below one `rg -n` call.
- **A rule this replaces.** A test asserted that block code must never appear in rows. That assumed a separate `extract` command that does not exist (its hint was removed with the diagnostics rework), so the rule left agents with nothing to read. The whole block is still not printed; only matching lines are.
- **Rejected.** Printing each block's `code`, as Part 1's snapshot lists: a large block costs more than the question needs, and the budget would have to count printed bytes. A separate `extract` command: a second call for every hit.
- **Open.** `--max-tokens` and `--max-bytes` still count the blocks the printed rows cover, not the snippets printed. Snippets are at most about 500 bytes a row, so the gap is small; counting printed bytes is the follow-up.
- **Superseded in 28 and 37.** The open item closed in 28. `--max-bytes` was removed in 37.
## 27. Tokens are estimated, not tokenized (2026-11-08)

- **Decision.** `count_tokens` returns the printed text's byte length divided by three, rounded up, and the `tiktoken-rs` dependency is gone. `--max-tokens` keeps its default of 20,000.
- **Why.** Building the `o200k_base` vocabulary took about 55 ms on the first row of any search with a match, against about 6 ms for the rest of the search: a match cost 50 ms where `rg` costs 9 (zustand, release build). On 15 real outputs from the pinned repos `o200k_base` ran 2.97 to 3.57 bytes per token (mean 3.34), so `ceil(bytes / 3)` reads about 11% high on average and never more than 1% low. The cap is a backstop: the worst output measured was 11 KB, about 3,000 tokens, and `--max-results` usually binds first. No vocabulary is the one every reader uses, so the exact count was exact for the wrong tokenizer.
- **Also removed.** The 32 KiB byte cap that kept quadratic BPE merging away from minified rows has no purpose without a tokenizer.
- **Rejected.** Keeping the tokenizer and building it on a thread while text search runs: it hides the cost on large repositories only, keeps the dependency and the binary size, and keeps counting with the wrong vocabulary. Rejected: `bytes / 4`, which reads about 17% low on these outputs and so lets a response overspend its cap.
- **Supersedes.** Part 8 §9.1 (byte length as a proven upper bound on tokens) still holds as a bound; the count now uses a tighter ratio and gives up the guarantee that it never understates.

## 51. michi 0.10.0: a cut cell ends in `…` and is listed in a `truncated` block (2026-11-16)

- **Decision.** `michi-core` moves from 0.7.1 to 0.10.0. The output keeps michi's cut-cell form and adds nothing: no `budget:` or `provenance:` block, no `truncation_hint`, no per-cell cap change. monokl does not cut cells itself.
- **What changes on the wire.** A cell over michi's 200-character cap used to end in `(N more chars ...)`. It now keeps 199 characters, ends in `…`, and a `truncated[N]{row,field,removed}:` block after the rows lists each cut (`row` is 0-based, `removed` is the characters cut). Only `symbolSignature` can reach the cap, because the snippet lines are already cut at 160 characters by monokl. The rest of the output is byte-identical.
- **Measured.** 23 of the 222 harness outputs (10%) carry the block. The total output is 385,471 bytes, was 383,506 at the last measure on main (+0.5%, about +85 bytes on an affected output). The harness holds: identifiers 59/59, questions 17/18, members 15/16, Rust 22/24, held-out 32/33, 22/22 and 35/36, answerable in one turn 206/222.
- **Why accept it.** The block is michi's definition of a cut and says what the reader did not get; the old suffix could not be told from a signature that ended that way. Cutting in monokl would hand-roll what michi provides (AGENTS.md) and drop the count. The cost is small and falls on the longest signatures.
- **Rejected.** Raising the cap to avoid the block: a longer signature costs more on every row that has one, to save the block on a few. Cutting the signature in monokl before michi sees it: no block, but the reader cannot tell a cut signature from a whole one. Adding `truncation_hint`: it tells the reader to pass `full=true`, which monokl has no flag for.
- **Not adopted from 0.10.0.** `BudgetSummary` and `ProvenanceBlock` cost about 66 tokens a response (+13% on the 509-token mean of a 20-query sample) and replace no line. Their types are marked unstable by michi until a second consumer uses them. `Section` is used for the one `search` list, which is how `total_count` is set now that `AgentResponse::total_count` is gone. `PartialSuccess` is per operation of a batch; a search has no operations.
